_note: A real sitting, shown on the day-one opening screen so the finished artifact is visible without a key. The answers are Alston Wang's own words, written 2026-11-24 and split across the four questions by the paragraphs he wrote them in. The model's turn — the three follow-ups, the withheld one, and the naming — was produced by applying demo/dispatch-followup-prompt.txt and demo/dispatch-name-prompt.txt verbatim, in a Claude Code session rather than by the deployed page. answers.question: What is taking up most of your mind right now?
answers.answer: It's a terrifying thought to think about how my parents gave birth to my sister at the age of 26. I am 28 now, and I am not where I want to be in life. I recognize I am fortunate to have family, friends, and a community, but sometimes I feel like an impostor hiding amongst the crowd. I have formed bad habits and insecurities that I am working on, and I hope the version of me when I turn 30 can say I am proud to eliminate those from my life.
answers.followup: You wrote that you hope you can say you eliminated them. Which one are you least sure about?
answers.followupAnswer: I am writing to keep myself accountable for eliminating bad habits.
answers.why: He named the habits in the plural and the hope in the singular; the gap is where the work is.

answers.question: What are you pretending to be fine about?
answers.answer: After the recent layoffs, I have been keeping my head high, putting my best foot forward. But those are days that I get up and feel directionless, and those are probably the darkest days. However, I look back at my life and the gratitude of being in this position keeps me going, searching for higher purposes.
answers.why: The layoffs are recent and he is still inside this one; those days are not material to mine.

answers.question: What do you want Alston to know about who you are at 28?
answers.answer: The 28-year-old today version of me is lost, but proud to be lost, because I can fantasize about the kind of life I want to live in the future, and work towards the goal. I felt young three years ago, and I still feel young today.
answers.followup: You said you can fantasize about the kind of life you want. What's in it?
answers.why: Pride in being lost rests on the fantasy; he described the pride but never the fantasy.

answers.question: What are you still deciding?
answers.answer: I am still deciding whether to relocate from Seattle to NYC for a clean restart. My family has gotten my back all these years, and perhaps it's my turn to give back.
answers.followup: You called it a clean restart. What is it in Seattle you would be restarting from?
answers.followupAnswer: I have been living selfishly for myself the last five years. Now it's time to give back to those who gave to me.
answers.why: He named where he would go and called it clean, but not what he would be leaving.

naming.title: Proud to be lost
naming.why: Three of the four answers circle the same gap between where he is and where he assumed he would be by now — his parents at 26, the impostor among the crowd, a restart he has not taken. The name is his own phrasing: he wrote "lost, but proud to be lost", and the pride is carrying as much weight in that sentence as the lostness.
naming.lede: At twenty-eight, in the months after the layoffs, he was measuring himself against his parents at twenty-six and had decided that being lost was not the same as being stuck.

_rejectedFollowups.question: You chose 26 as the comparison. What were your parents doing at 28 — the age you are now?
You said you felt young three years ago. What were you doing then?

_rejectedNote: These two were the first follow-ups the prompt generated, and the author rejected both as irrelevant. Each turned on a number he had used as a measuring stick rather than on what he was measuring. The prompt was corrected (TRADEOFFS T-39) and re-run; the questions below are the second attempt.
